messages:
sarah_sales: Quick heads-up — Nimbus Health is evaluating Redwood Private. They need an on-prem environment to call our VPC endpoints without any public-facing ingress. Question is: recommend VPC peering, PrivateLink, or a site-to-site VPN + proxy? They care about latency (~50ms target), predictable egress, and strict firewall rules.

jon_eng: Thanks. A few clarifying Qs before a call: how many on-prem datacenters? expected concurrent connections? do they require mutual TLS or client certs?

anna_it: Hi — we have two DCs (NY and CHI), ~250 concurrent connections during peak, mutual TLS preferred, and we need to restrict egress IPs for allowlisting.

keith_net: TL;DR: If they need per-service private endpoints and strict allowlist w/o asymmetric routing, PrivateLink is simplest. For multi-VPC/multi-account routing or central transit, TGW + static routes works better. VPN introduces NAT/throughput overhead but can be simpler if they already have IPSec.

keith_net: Some practical trade-offs: 
- PrivateLink: no cross-AZ IP routing needed on customer side, supports NLB in front of the service, easier firewall rules (allow traffic to endpoint ENIs). But requires us to publish an interface endpoint per region/service.
- VPC Peering: low latency, but peering doesn't transit across peered VPCs (scale problem) and requires route table changes and careful SG rules.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPSec) to a bastion/proxy: gives customer full control of egress IPs but adds NAT and could increase latency jitter.

jon_eng: For mutual TLS we usually terminate on our side at the proxy/NLB layer — we can accept client certs to validate customer. PrivateLink + NLB + mTLS on our NGINX/gateway is doable.

emma_sec: One security note: PrivateLink ENIs live in our VPC — customer cannot see our subnets. Make sure to document which ENI IP ranges we will allocate for endpoint services so they can update their firewall ACLs.

keith_net: Sample firewall rules the customer asked for — give them this template: 
``` 
# Allow outbound to Redwood PrivateLink ENIs (example)
ALLOW TCP 443 FROM 10.0.0.0/16 TO 172.31.10.0/24
# If using VPN -> proxy, allow ephemeral replies
ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 FROM 10.0.0.0/16 TO 203.0.113.45
# ICMP (for troubleshooting)
ALLOW ICMP FROM 10.0.0.0/16 TO 172.31.10.0/24
``` 
(Replace CIDRs with final ENI ranges we provide).

anna_it: Nice. For the VPN/proxy option, can you confirm our egress IPs so we can push them to our perimeter firewalls?

jon_eng: If we go PrivateLink we provide endpoint ENI ranges per region — static for the duration of the POC. If VPN/proxy we can offer a small set of NATed egress IPs (we'll commit those in the contract). Which is preferable depends on their ops model.

keith_net: Also note MTU/fragmentation — if they run IPSec, ensure their edge devices allow 1380-1420 byte MTU or enable path MTU to avoid TLS fragmentation.

sarah_sales: Cost note for Nimbus — PrivateLink will have hourly ENI and NLB costs per region; TGW has attachment + data processing. We'll include a rough delta in the POC pricing doc.

anna_it: Understood. Next steps: can we get a one-pager with recommended architecture + firewall template + list of IP ranges we might use for the POC? Also a 30-min tech call tomorrow afternoon if possible.

jon_eng: I'll assemble a one-pager and a tidy diagram.

keith_net: I'll draft the firewall template and a checklist (routes, SG, subnet planning).

emma_sec: I'll review the one-pager for compliance flags (e.g., external audit trail for PrivateLink usage).

infra_bot: deploy-bot: reminder — please attach the internal diagram to the sales ticket: https://redwood.example/pipelines/PR-4823 (auto-note).

sarah_sales: Great — locking 15:00 ET tomorrow for the tech call. I'll invite Nimbus IT + our SEs. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jon_eng: Copy — will bring mTLS config example and NLB listener snippet: 
``` 
listener 443 {
  ssl_preread on;
  ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/redwood.pem;
  client_certificate /etc/ssl/nimbus-ca.pem;
  verify_client on;
}
``` 

keith_net: FYI I'll also include a minimal route table diff they can apply for peering vs VPN so ops has a checklist.

anna_it: Perfect, thanks everyone.
